To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) dietary assessment methods have a variety of uses; 2) dietary assessment methods vary in their validity and reliability; 3) the validity and reliability of a given assessment method depend on the purpose of the assessment; 4) dietary intake is a multidimensional construct; 5) the validity of a given assessment tool depends on the construct being measured; and 6) the validity of any assessment tool depends on how it is administered.
the use of a dietary assessment tool in a specific study design is not necessarily the best approach, but it can be a useful one, depending on the study goal.
the validity of self-reported dietary data is supported by a large and growing body of research and that the use of such data in epidemiological studies is supported by a growing body of evidence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between behavior and health.
the relationship between dietary patterns, food intake, and the health of individuals and populations.
the development and evaluation of dietary assessment instruments, the application of these tools to population studies, and the interpretation of the results of these studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the validity of recall-based measures is a function of their design, the study in which they are used, and the goal of the study.

“recalls are not perfect but they are the best we have.” We agree with Archer et al that the use of dietary assessment tools in epidemiological studies is fraught with challenges, but we disagree with the conclusion that dietary assessment tools are invalid and therefore should not be used to establish the relationship between diet and health.
the validity of self-reported data is dependent on the context of the study, the purpose of the study, and the quality of the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the more detailed the recall, the more valid it is.
, when we have a choice, we prefer to eat healthy foods, but we do not always do so.
, when we have the ability to collect objective measures of behavior, they provide the most valid and reliable estimates of the true exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recall-based assessment can be a useful tool to investigate the relationship between dietary behaviors and health outcomes.
recall-based assessments can be used to develop evidence that supports the use of dietary guidelines to improve public health, and we provide evidence to support this conclusion.
recall measures can provide a valid representation of behavior.
